questions.q: Why is the concept of a 'storage engine' something a T-SQL developer has never had to think about?
options: SQL Server uses one underlying storage mechanism for every table, with no per-table engine choice
T-SQL doesn't support CREATE TABLE at all
SQL Server has storage engines too, just under a different name
Storage engines only matter for read-only reporting tables
questions.explain: MySQL is architected to support multiple, swappable storage engines per table; SQL Server has no equivalent per-table choice to make.

questions.q: What does InnoDB support that MyISAM does not?
options: Full-text search only
Transactions, foreign key constraints, and row-level locking
Faster table creation speed only
Case-insensitive column names
questions.explain: InnoDB is the modern default specifically because it supports the transactional, referential, and concurrency features developers expect.

questions.q: What happens if application code runs ROLLBACK after a failed operation that modified a MyISAM table?
options: The MyISAM table's changes are NOT rolled back — MyISAM never participated in the transaction
MyISAM automatically converts itself to InnoDB to allow the rollback
ROLLBACK works identically regardless of engine
The entire database refuses to process the ROLLBACK and throws an error
questions.explain: This is the real, silent failure mode: MyISAM has no transaction support, so ROLLBACK simply does nothing for that table's changes.

questions.q: Which commands reveal a MySQL table's storage engine?
options: SHOW TABLE STATUS and SHOW CREATE TABLE
There is no way to check a table's engine after creation
DESCRIBE TABLE ENGINE
SELECT * FROM information_schema.engines only
questions.explain: Both SHOW TABLE STATUS and SHOW CREATE TABLE expose the table's engine, letting you verify it before writing transactional code.

questions.q: Why does a table's storage engine matter to a developer, not just a DBA?
options: It changes the SQL SELECT syntax required to query the table
It only affects how fast backups run, which is purely an operations concern
It has no practical effect on anything application-level
Code that assumes transactional behavior (like ROLLBACK) will silently misbehave on a MyISAM table
questions.explain: This is the chapter's key developer-relevant point: engine choice silently changes whether your error-handling and transaction code actually works.
